subject: Film & Cinema
title: What Is Animation?
description: A 60-second lesson on What Is Animation?.

hook.text: Animation is the illusion of movement. Your brain sees still images and invents motion.

buildup.text: At 24 frames per second, separate drawings blur into fluid movement.

discovery.text: Persistence of vision — the brain holds an image briefly after it disappears — makes animation possible.

twist.text: Animation isn't just cartoons. It's any technique that creates movement from still elements.

climax.text: From cave paintings to CGI, humans have always tried to make still images come alive.

punchline.text: Animation is the oldest trick the brain falls for.

quiz.question: What optical principle makes animation possible?
options: Persistence of vision — the brain retains images briefly
